transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As you know, I've got those three unlabeled Hi8 tapes from the late '90s at home, and I need to put together a plan for how we'll transfer them to digital, store the originals, and make copies available to the family. Before I decide on anything, I want to do our usual check-in — please share whatever you know or anything you think needs to be considered about these tapes. I know they've got family gatherings on them and a recording from inside our grandparents' old house, but I'm sure some of you might have additional context or concerns. So, what do you know?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important. I spoke with Aunt Celia recently, and she asked that tape 03 never be shared beyond her and Jordan. She said it includes a private conversation. This request hasn't reached the rest of the family until now, so I wanted to make sure it's on the table before Jordan puts together the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've got something that should help with the transfer plan. I own a working Digital8/Hi8 camcorder that can play these tapes and transfer them directly to a computer. So we don't need to send the tapes out to a general conversion service — we can handle the transfer ourselves, which I think is better anyway since it keeps the originals in the family the whole time.

My archival contact recommended creating the digital masters as FFV1-encoded Matroska files, storing the originals in an acid-free box kept between 18 and 21 degrees Celsius, and transferring tape 02 first because it is the most fragile.
